html:
On 3 November 1988 about eighty armed men of a Sri Lankan Tamil group, hired by a Maldivian businessman, landed at Male by boat and tried to overthrow President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom.

They seized parts of the capital, but Gayoom hid and called for help. India sent paratroopers within hours, in Operation Cactus. The airport was retaken, the coup collapsed, and an Indian navy ship caught the fleeing gunmen at sea with hostages.

The attack showed how easily a few dozen fighters could threaten a state of scattered islands with almost no army. It tied the Maldives closely to India for a generation. Later governments swung between India and China, a rivalry that still shapes the islands' politics.
sum: On 3 November 1988 about eighty armed men of a Sri Lankan Tamil group, hired by a Maldivian businessman, landed at Male by boat and tried to overthrow President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom.
